About the Emergency Medical Technician event

Emergency Medical Technician is a Emergency Preparedness event in the HOSA secondary division. Format: testing · skills.

Ten in-depth lessons for the two-person HOSA Emergency Medical Technician event, following the 2026–27 test plan (patient assessment 20%, basic life support 20%, trauma 16%, pediatrics and childbirth 16%, medical emergencies 14%, environmental emergencies 10%, special situations 4%) and all nine Round Two skills: trauma and medical patient assessment, BVM ventilation of an apneic adult, long bone or joint immobilization, bleeding control and shock management, cardiac arrest management with AED, oxygen by non-rebreather mask, epinephrine auto-injector and naloxone. Built around Emergency Care and Transportation of the Sick and Injured, the AHA BLS Provider Manual and Brady Emergency Care, with DCAP-BTLS, OPQRST and SAMPLE drills, vital-sign and glucose labs, rhythm recognition, START triage sorting and scenario decisions. Always follow the scenario you are given and your local protocols.

Emergency Medical Technician practice tests

Each test is an original, full-length simulation of the HOSA Round One written test, written to run slightly harder than the real thing. Every answer comes with an explanation and a reference.

Sample Emergency Medical Technician questions

1. Why does the AHA recommend switching compressors about every 2 minutes during CPR?

  1. Fatigue reduces compression quality
  2. The AED requires it to analyze
  3. It allows the pulse to be checked
  4. Compressions cause rib fractures after 2 minutes
Show answer

A. Fatigue reduces compression quality

Rescuers become fatigued within a couple of minutes, often without noticing, and compressions become shallower. Switching at each rhythm check keeps compressions effective.

2. What is the maximum time an adult’s airway should be suctioned at one time?

  1. 5 seconds
  2. 30 seconds
  3. 15 seconds
  4. 60 seconds
Show answer

C. 15 seconds

Suctioning removes oxygen along with secretions, so adults are suctioned no longer than 15 seconds at a time (less for children and infants), with oxygen between attempts.

3. How often should an unstable patient be reassessed during transport?

  1. Every 10 minutes
  2. Every 5 minutes
  3. Every 15 minutes
  4. Only on arrival at the hospital
Show answer

B. Every 5 minutes

Unstable patients are reassessed at least every 5 minutes and stable patients at least every 15 minutes, or after every intervention.
